2x.note: same coordinates (all manifest numbers are 1x canvas px); draw @2x tiles at 0.5 scale. Use on >=2x screens when the bot is drawn wider than ~320 px.

coordinate_system: top-left XY; +X right, +Y down; clockwise-positive degrees; column-vector affine matrices; all numbers in 1x canvas px
paint_composite_order: mask alpha tinted to paint token
alpha: straight/unassociated RGBA PNG; sRGB; no baked background
mirror: Mirror the complete assembled hierarchy about x=320 (x_new = 640 - x). Never flip tiles independently. l/r = view-left(rear)/view-right(front).
hierarchy_note: hand_l_wrap/hand_r_wrap are children of their hand (socket "wrap" = hand pivot, angle 0). The equipped weapon is a child of hand_r.grip.

sword.draw_order_note: hand back layer < weapon < hand *_wrap layer for every gripping hand

axe.draw_order_note: hand back layer < weapon < hand *_wrap layer for every gripping hand
axe.off_grip_released_reason: victory raises the axe one-handed (two-handed overhead does not fit the rig reach/canvas); defeat lets go with the rear hand. In every other pose the off hand is on grip_off.
axe.off_hand_rule: hand_l is NOT parented to the weapon. Every pose ships baked hand_l rotations that land hand_l.grip on weapon_axe.grip_off (validated <= 1.5 px / 2 deg). If an engine blends poses, blend all rots; do not re-solve.

dagger.draw_order_note: hand back layer < weapon < hand *_wrap layer for every gripping hand
dagger.grip_style_reason: Reverse (ice-pick) grip: blade leaves the little-finger side and angles down toward the opponent. At fight scale it gives the dagger a silhouette that cannot be mistaken for a short sword, and its guard reads as a raised fist.

assets.note: curled fingers/thumb drawn OVER the weapon handle; same tile/pivot as its hand; always drawn
curled fingers/thumb drawn OVER the weapon handle; same tile/pivot as its hand; always drawn
child of hand_r.grip; pivot = own grip_main socket; angle = attach_angle. Draw only the equipped weapon.
child of hand_r.grip; pivot = own grip_main socket; angle = attach_angle. Draw only the equipped weapon.
child of hand_r.grip; pivot = own grip_main socket; angle = attach_angle. Draw only the equipped weapon.

idle.use: stable / customise / fight idle. Per-weapon guard.

victory.use: result overlay, own bot. Weapon raised, chest out, rear fist pumped.

defeat.use: result overlay / KO hold. Both knees down, slumped, head hanging, weapon grounded.

portrait.use: ranking head-and-shoulders portrait source pose; render WITHOUT weapon

quick_attack.use: v002 delta re-based onto the v003 per-weapon guard; axe two-handed re-solved. Not re-art-directed.

heavy_windup.use: v002 delta re-based onto the v003 per-weapon guard; axe two-handed re-solved. Not re-art-directed.

heavy_attack.use: v002 delta re-based onto the v003 per-weapon guard; axe two-handed re-solved. Not re-art-directed.

dodge.use: v002 delta re-based onto the v003 per-weapon guard; axe two-handed re-solved. Not re-art-directed.

hit.use: v002 delta re-based onto the v003 per-weapon guard; axe two-handed re-solved. Not re-art-directed.

pose_format.rot: degrees ADDED to the part's default `angle`, rotating around its own pivot. Missing part = 0. torso.rot is the root rotation.
pose_format.weapon: never posed directly; it follows hand_r via grips.main.attach_angle
pose_format.blend: linear interpolation of root.x/y and each rot is valid between any two entries of the same weapon

defeat_sparks.orientation: screen-up (position follows the socket; do not inherit torso rotation)
defeat_sparks.playback: optional one-shot on KO hold; frames 00-02 then hide; static frame 01 for reduced motion or skip

portrait.facing: right (canonical); mirror only if the row layout requires it
portrait.filter: render the full 640 assembly at >= 2x parts, then crop and Lanczos-downsample
portrait.note: crop is anchored to the world position of torso.neck in the portrait pose, so any future head/torso part or paint keeps the framing

mapping.reducedMotion: snap to the target pose, no tween; result plates still shown

validation_summary.meaning: Geometry/file/raster proof from manifest + PNGs. Not art acceptance, native performance, animation timing or full collision clearance.
